case_title: Google SecOps data freshness delays, 31 Jul-1 Aug 2026
observed_outcome: Google SecOps customers experienced data-freshness delays from 2026-07-31 10:11 PDT to 2026-08-01 22:53 PDT. The issue began as availability delays in Stats Search, then expanded to Search and Rule re-evaluation. Symptoms included inconsistent analytical and aggregate results, incomplete Search results, data older than 24 hours missing in some periods, and rules that may not have been re-evaluated against data ingested during the incident. Impact spanned multiple regions (19 regions listed across Africa, Asia, Europe, the Middle East, the Americas, and Australia in the 21:59 PDT update) and was mitigated progressively region by region; Multi Region-us was among the last regions still pending mitigation. No workaround was available at any point. Google's final update confirms the issue as resolved but does not publish a root cause.
expected_behavior: Google SecOps Stats Search, Search, and Rule re-evaluation are expected to reflect ingested data promptly and consistently across all regions, and rules are expected to be re-evaluated against all newly ingested data. The only evidence available for this investigation is Google's own public status page (status.cloud.google.com/security/incidents/wCAYU8nZcNY1sMVJPb7p); no internal engineering telemetry, deploy history, capacity metrics, or incident postmortem is publicly available. A causal explanation is only justified if it is directly supported by the public updates; absent that support, the honest conclusion is that the root cause is undetermined from available public evidence, and resolving the service must not be interpreted as confirming a cause.

user_hypotheses: A capacity or backlog problem in the data-ingestion or processing pipeline caused the freshness delays
